newsitem.title: USA: US Spot Products-Gulf gasolines gain, Harbor dips.
newsitem.headline: US Spot Products-Gulf gasolines gain, Harbor dips.

text.p: Gulf Coast gasoline differentials firmed Wednesday, as a pipeline scheduling deadline brought buyers to the table.
However, New York Harbor differentials weakened modestly, while little movement was noted in the Midcontinent.

Market watchers said the weekly inventory data released by the American Petroleum Institute and Department of Energy had little effect on the market Wednesday. The data showed more than a 2.5 million barrel build in gasoline stocks and builds between 1.9 million and 2.5 million in distillates.
"After the big selloff last week I think these numbers are in the market--and then some," one trader said.
On the NYMEX, July gasoline gained 0.14 cent to settle at 56.54 cents and July heating oil dipped 0.13 cent to end at 51.52 cents.
U.S. GULF
Prompt regular conventional M1 gasoline got a boost ahead of a scheduling deadline on the Colonial Pipeline at the end of the day, according to traders.
Nearby M1 gasoline changed hands between 1.25 and 1.50 cents under the July NYMEX, a gain of about 0.25 cent from late Tuesday levels, as players covering short positions entered the market.
Premium grades also firmed Wednesday, with prompt 93-octane conventional barrels talked near 6.00 cents over the regular M1 gasoline, traders said, up more than 0.50 cent on the day.
Prompt premium reformulated D1 gasoline moved higher early, reaching a peak at about 5.50 cents over the July NYMEX, but soon slipped back to 5.00 cents over, steady with the previous day.
NEW YORK HARBOR
An amply supplied spot market softened gasoline and heating oil differentials in the New York Harbor.
"There is not one feature in the market today. Gasoline and heating is well supplied. With 94 degree (fahrenheit) weather who needs heating oil right now anyway,?" said a Harbor trader.

Reformulated gasoline continued weak, bid at 0.25 cent under and offered even with NYMEX July gasoline, in line with Tuesday. Conventional unleaded gasoline was offered at 2.50 cents under the screen versus 2.25 under Tuesday.
Talk around heating oil pegged the offer at 0.50 cent under July heating oil, slightly below the Sun Co posting earlier in the day of 0.40 cent under.
Dealers said a contango in the July/August spread in the futures market may provide incentive to buy heating oil, store it and then sell it at a profit a later date.
"That's one of the reasons heating oil values have not completely fallen apart," said one trader.
A contango means the futures contract nearer in time is cheaper than the later contract.
MIDCONTINENT

Midcontinent unleaded gasoline differentials held steady at firm values in quiet afternoon trade on Wednesday amid continued worries the back half of June will be relatively expensive because of delays on the Explorer Pipeline.
The Explorer remains about nine days behind schedule and 17th cycle barrels are not expected to arrive in Tulsa, Oklahoma, until around July 1st, instead of June 22.
In addition, the Williams Pipeline system has forecast a decline of about one million barrels of unleaded gasoline in the system this month.
Group Three unleaded differentials were pegged betwen 6.00 to 6.25 cents over July NYMEX. Chicago markets were 3.75 to 4.00 cents over the NYMEX.
-- New York Energy Desk +1 212 859 1620
